_metadata.independence: I read only u13-blind-input.json and no other file, search result, web page or API before scoring.

hints.reason: Shared property: a house cat's whiskers and a lion's whiskers are the same familiar feature.
Compound route: 'big cat' is the familiar phrase, and the lion is the archetypal big cat.

best_available.why: Reaches both words directly through one physical feature every player can picture.

pairs.pair_note: Easy pair; both hints are clean.

hints.reason: Shared scene: the moon belongs to the night, and the nocturnal cat prowling or silhouetted under it is a stock image.

best_available.why: A single familiar scene (cat out at night under the moon) covers both words.

pairs.pair_note: Cat side is a little softer than the moon side but the scene is well known.

hints.reason: Compound 'alley cat' for the cat; a dark alley at night is the stock setting for the night side.
Verb route: cats prowl, and prowling is a night-time activity ('on the prowl at night', 'night prowler').

best_available.why: The verb binds the two words in one action rather than two separate images.

pairs.pair_note: Both work; night side leans on atmosphere in each case.

hints.reason: Ship on the ocean is direct; the cat side is the traditional ship's cat kept aboard by sailors, a recognizable scene comparable to TREAT for APPLE+HORSE.

best_available.why: Only hint, and the ship's-cat tradition is familiar enough to make it fair.

pairs.pair_note: Cat side depends on the ship's cat; players who do not know it will see SHIP as one-sided.

hints.reason: Compound 'cat's eye' (marbles, glasses, slit pupils) for the cat; the pirate's eye patch for the pirate.
Pirate ship is a stock compound; the cat side is the ship's cat tradition.

best_available.why: Both sides are instant and distinct images.

pairs.pair_note: EYE is the clear winner; SHIP is serviceable.

hints.reason: Cleopatra is a famous queen; the cat side runs through two hops (Cleopatra -> ancient Egypt -> sacred cats, plus the 'cat eye' eyeliner look), which a player may not make unaided.
Ancient Egypt's cat worship is widely known; Egypt's queens (Cleopatra, Nefertiti) supply the queen side.

best_available.why: Cat-worshipping Egypt is a direct, widely known link and Cleopatra is a famous queen.

pairs.pair_note: EGYPT carries the pair; CLEOPATRA reaches the cat only through Egypt.

hints.reason: Cat's tail is direct, but ring reaches tail only through 'ring-tailed' (lemur, ringtail cat), a phrase a player would not recover from TAIL alone.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; it is one-sided but the only candidate.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Pair needs a new hint (e.g. BELL for a cat's collar bell / bell ring, or BOXING for cat fight / boxing ring).

hints.reason: Robot vacuum (Roomba) is direct; the cat riding or fleeing the vacuum is a well-known internet scene.

best_available.why: One widely shared scene (cat on a Roomba) that contains both words.

pairs.pair_note: Good single hint.

hints.reason: Pet cat is direct; the famous novelty 'pet rock' gives the rock side.

best_available.why: Compound on both sides with a satisfying twist.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Cats scratch; rose thorns scratch you when you pick them, a shared verb/property.

best_available.why: A single shared verb that fits both naturally.

pairs.pair_note: Fine.

hints.reason: Cats lick themselves; 'salt lick' is the compound for the salt side.

best_available.why: Verb on one side, familiar compound on the other.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Cats sneak; 'sneaking in the shadows' is the stock phrase for the shadow side.
'Black cat' is a strong compound; shadows are dark/black, a shared-property route.

best_available.why: Binds the words in one action; BLACK is a colour route but still fair.

pairs.pair_note: Both acceptable; colour flag on BLACK is informational only.

hints.reason: A tiger is a big cat; 'tiger shark' is a well-known species.

best_available.why: Clean on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Both animals hiss; a shared behaviour everyone knows.

best_available.why: Direct shared behaviour.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Catwoman is a household name; Spider-Woman is a real Marvel character and players reach it from Spider-Man even if they have not met her.

best_available.why: Superhero-name route on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Spider side slightly weaker than the cat side but recoverable.

hints.reason: Cats pounce; spring as the verb 'to leap' is near-synonymous with pounce, an allowed verb route.

best_available.why: The cat's spring/pounce is one motion.

pairs.pair_note: Relies on the verb sense of SPRING, not the season or coil.

hints.reason: Leo is a star sign/constellation; Leo is the lion, a big cat.

best_available.why: Zodiac lion covers both words.

pairs.pair_note: Cat side goes through lion, but Leo-the-lion is widely known.

hints.reason: Cat litter is direct; 'litter-train' / 'litter-trained' uses train as a verb, an allowed inflection route.

best_available.why: A familiar compound-verb (litter-training a cat) that contains both words.

pairs.pair_note: Train side is the verb, not the locomotive.

hints.reason: Cats famously hate baths; bath water is direct.

best_available.why: A single shared scene (bathing a reluctant cat).

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Shared property: both animals are furred.
Shared property: both are hunting predators.

best_available.why: Slightly more specific than FUR while still reaching both.

pairs.pair_note: Both broad but valid under the rubric; generic is a flag, not a rejection.

hints.reason: A diamond is 'set' in a mount; a crown is set with gems, but the crown side is reached only by picturing the diamond already in the crown, and SET is a very broad word for a player to decode.
Diamonds sparkle; a jewelled crown sparkles, a shared property.
'Crown jewels' is the compound; a diamond is a jewel.

best_available.why: Compound on the crown side and a direct category on the diamond side.

pairs.pair_note: JEWEL is strong; SET is a stretch on the crown side.

hints.reason: Crown-king is direct; the dog side rests on 'King' as a common dog name and the King Charles spaniel, which a player may not land on.
Royal crown is direct; the dog side runs through the Queen's royal corgis or the Royal Canin brand, both a step removed.

best_available.why: King Charles spaniel and the dog name 'King' give it a slightly firmer dog foothold than ROYAL.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Both hints are crown-first with a thin dog side; CORGI-style routes are the natural fix (e.g. CORGI itself is not a hint here).

hints.reason: Crown and throne are paired royal symbols; the dragon side is Game of Thrones, where dragons are central, a widely known story route.

best_available.why: Only hint; the Game of Thrones link is broad enough to carry the dragon.

pairs.pair_note: Dragon side depends on one franchise, but a very famous one.

hints.reason: Faberge eggs are famous; the crown side is that they were made for the Russian imperial crown (the Tsars) and are jewelled like crowns, which many players know only vaguely.

best_available.why: Only hint; the imperial-egg link is real and moderately known.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Defensible as a reach but not clean; a second opinion is worthwhile.

hints.reason: Gold crown is direct; fire reaches gold only via 'refined by fire' or a loose colour resemblance, neither of which a player would see.
'Ring of fire' is a familiar phrase; a crown is a ring-shaped circlet of jewellery, but a player is unlikely to move from RING to CROWN without prompting.
Candle flame is direct; the crown side (St Lucia candle crown, Advent crown) is too obscure to count.

best_available.why: The only hint with a plausible, if thin, route to both (ring of fire; crown as a ring).

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The pair wants a shared scene such as a dragon or a phoenix; none of these hints supply it.

hints.reason: Crown-king is direct; kingfish, king salmon, king mackerel and the kingfisher give the fish side via familiar compounds.

best_available.why: Compound route on the fish side is real and reasonably known.

pairs.pair_note: Acceptable; fish side is compound-dependent.

hints.reason: Crystal glass/glassware is direct; crowns and tiaras are studded with crystals, a shared-material route.

best_available.why: Material shared by both objects.

pairs.pair_note: Fine.

hints.reason: King Midas wore the crown; his golden touch is the gold side.
Crown-king is direct; the gold side (a king's gold, royal treasury) is reached mostly through the crown itself rather than independently.

best_available.why: One story that names both a crowned king and gold.

pairs.pair_note: MIDAS is excellent; KING is a judgement call that leans crown-only.

hints.reason: The knight piece is a horse; the king and queen pieces wear crowns.
The 'Triple Crown' of horse racing contains both words in one compound.
Horse-drawn carriage is direct; the royal carriage (coronation procession) gives the crown side.

best_available.why: Both words sit in one famous phrase.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair.

hints.reason: A queen wears a crown; 'ice queen' is a familiar compound.
Elsa's ice powers are direct; her coronation as queen of Arendelle in Frozen gives the crown side.

best_available.why: Compound and role in one word.

pairs.pair_note: Both good; ELSA is a story route.

hints.reason: 'The Man in the Iron Mask' is a known title; the crown side (the masked prisoner is the king's twin, a plot about the throne) needs the story explained.
Crown and throne are paired symbols; the Iron Throne of Game of Thrones gives the iron side.
'Iron fist' is the compound; the crown side is only the idiom 'rule with an iron fist', so the player must infer a monarch.

best_available.why: Compound on the iron side and a direct royal pairing on the crown side.

pairs.pair_note: THRONE carries the pair; MASK and FIST are iron-first.

hints.reason: The Tower of London holds the Crown Jewels (moderate); the key side would be the Ceremony of the Keys, which almost no player would reach.
Lock and key is direct; there is no recognizable route from LOCK to CROWN.
A crown rules a kingdom; 'keys to the kingdom' is a familiar idiom (and Kingdom Hearts for gamers).

best_available.why: The idiom binds both words.

pairs.pair_note: KINGDOM is strong; TOWER and LOCK are filler.

hints.reason: Throne, crown and king are one royal scene.
Royal crown; a king is royalty.
The coronation is the ceremony where the crown is placed on the king.

best_available.why: Names the exact event joining the two words.

pairs.pair_note: Trivially easy pair; all three fine.

hints.reason: A king wears the crown and knights his knights (and both are chess pieces).
King Arthur wore the crown and led the Knights of the Round Table.

best_available.why: A single story containing a crowned king and his knights.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair.

hints.reason: Crown-king is direct; 'The Lion King' and 'king of the jungle' give the lion side.

best_available.why: Both sides immediate.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Princess Diana gives the crown side; Diana is the Roman goddess of the moon.
A halo is a crown-like ring worn on the head; a lunar halo is the ring of light around the moon, a shared-shape route.

best_available.why: Two famous referents, one royal and one lunar, in one name.

pairs.pair_note: HALO is a shape route with neither side at full strength; still fair.

hints.reason: Crown-king is direct; the mouse side is the Mouse King of The Nutcracker, known mainly to ballet audiences.

best_available.why: Only hint; the Nutcracker's Mouse King is a real but moderate route.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. MICKEY-style routes (Disney royalty) would be stronger but are not offered.

hints.reason: Prom king and queen are crowned; 'prom night' is the stock phrase.

best_available.why: One familiar scene with both words.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Neptune is the god/king of the sea; he is pictured crowned with his trident.
King Triton of The Little Mermaid is a crowned ruler of the ocean.

best_available.why: Broadest recognition; sea-king imagery includes the crown.

pairs.pair_note: Both sea-king routes; fine.

hints.reason: Pirate treasure is direct; a jewelled crown is a classic item in the treasure chest (and the Crown Jewels are literally treasure).

best_available.why: A single stock image (treasure chest with a crown on top) contains both.

pairs.pair_note: Fine.
